pains.title: Nobody knows what each clinician earns the practice
pains.problem: Clinician pay is the largest cost, and splits rarely get revisited while payer rates stay flat. Without books by clinician, you cannot tell which hires make money.
pains.how: Lucid reports collected revenue, pay, payroll tax and overhead per clinician each month. Your CPA then checks your pay model against those numbers, by location too.

pains.title: Busy, but short on cash
pains.problem: Groups that mix insurance and private pay carry large gaps between billed and collected, and slow payers hide inside one total.
pains.how: Lucid does not file claims or chase insurance, your biller does that. Lucid keeps books by payer, reconciles deposits to the bank and tracks payer mix monthly.

pains.title: New hires cost money before insurance pays
pains.problem: A new clinician usually cannot bill insurance until credentialing finishes, so you pay wages while little insurance income arrives.
pains.how: Lucid builds that gap into your cash forecast, so you know the runway a hire needs. Lucid does not run credentialing.

faq_title: Behavioral health accounting questions group owners ask

faq.q: How do I know how much profit each therapist in my group practice makes?
faq.a: Your books need to track collected revenue and pay by clinician, not just in one lump. Lucid sets that up and gives you a monthly view of what each clinician brings in, what they cost with payroll tax and benefits, and what is left. That tells you whether a raise or a new hire makes sense before you commit.

faq.q: Should my therapists be W-2 employees or paid on a 1099?
faq.a: It depends on how much control you have over their schedule, methods and clients, and the rules differ by state. Lucid reviews how your clinicians are paid from the tax side and tells you where the risk looks high, so you can take it to your attorney. Lucid does not give legal advice.

faq.q: How much does it cost me to hire a therapist who is not credentialed yet?
faq.a: You pay their wages while insurance revenue is delayed, which often means months of cost before the first claim pays. Lucid builds that gap into your cash forecast so you know how much runway a new hire needs.

faq.q: What are the alternatives to Heard for a group practice with employees?
faq.a: As of November 2026, Heard says it supports single owner group practices and does not serve co-owned practices. Lucid serves groups with staff, several locations and owners with several practices, with a dedicated CPA on every account and published pricing. See the Lucid vs Heard comparison for the details.

faq.q: Does Lucid do my billing or chase insurance?
faq.a: No. Lucid works alongside your biller or billing software. Lucid handles the books, taxes and CFO reporting, and gives you clear numbers on payer mix and margin by clinician.
